verdict: APPROVE, no blockers. One divergence (R1) could drop valid device traffic if the device pads messages; fix it or give it a distinct error before relying on enumeration results.

revision_2.change: deliver() now requires declared payload + 10 <= n instead of ==. The CRC is still checked over n-2 bytes at n-2, and payload_length stays the declared length, so padding is never delivered. Header comment added; no API change.
revision_2.result: R1 FIXED. Root tests pass here (ASan+UBSan), including the new padded-accept and over-declared-refuse case. Differential vs the Linux model: 3000 random valid streams identical; 2842 random padded or over-declared streams (padding 0..200, 20% declared past the end, strides 246/200/123) identical, 0 differences. The padded case now matches Linux. Remaining divergences are unchanged and non-blocking: R2 (an unrelated invalid packet aborts a partial), short final fragments (superset), descriptor >512 (same outcome), R3 (BOOT ignores offset/remain, as in the reference).
revision_2.verdict: APPROVE for hardware use by the native adapter.

verified: CRC is CRC-16/ARC (reflected 0xA001, init 0, no xorout), matching Linux crc16(0, ...). Golden vector 0xBB3D.

Packet layout flags@0, device@1, offset@2, remain@4, length@6, data@8..253, crc@254; message header u0, u1, u2, id, rsplen, length; message CRC follows the payload. Request builder byte-matches the reference request layout; output is untouched on failure.

Every copy is bounded: the fragment is <= 246, offset+length+remain <= 2048 (the assembly buffer), continuation requires an exact offset, device, flags and constant total, and the delivered copy is <= 2048. This fixes the reference reassembly overflow (core.c:814/842).
Descriptor (flags 0x40, 0x20/0x10) payloads over 512 are refused; requests for it are capped at 512. Zero-length payloads are refused, as in the reference.
Valid single-packet messages interleaved inside a fragmented response leave it intact.
Root tests: all pass here with ASan and UBSan (2038 lengths, the interleave, the cap, refusals, 50000 malformed inputs).

Independent differential: 3000 random valid streams (1-4 messages, payload 1..2038, all devices and flags, random fragment strides, 30% interleaved single packets) gave identical delivered messages from root's engine (ctypes) and a Python model of the pinned Linux process_read/assemble/process_message.

divergences_from_reference.linux: drops it as a short packet, so the message never completes
divergences_from_reference.assessment: Root is a superset. That Linux works suggests the device avoids such fragments (inference).

divergences_from_reference.case: message length > payload+10 with the CRC at length-2 (padding)
divergences_from_reference.linux: accepts: CRC checked at length-2, payload_len+10 <= length (core.c:735-745)
divergences_from_reference.assessment: Only divergence that can drop valid traffic. Trailing bytes are still CRC-covered, so accepting them is safe. Either accept like Linux (and expose the trailing count), or use a distinct error code so the first hardware enumeration shows it unambiguously.

divergences_from_reference.case: invalid unrelated packet (bad packet CRC, short junk, bad single-message CRC) between fragments
divergences_from_reference.linux: keeps the partial and completes it
divergences_from_reference.assessment: Fail-closed and documented, but less robust. Keeping the partial on errors unrelated to the assembly is equally safe, because offset/identity/total continuity and the final message CRC still guard it. Optional.

divergences_from_reference.linux: delivered, then refused by the handler (core.c:688-689)

divergences_from_reference.case: CRC-valid 4-byte fragment equal to a0 80 00 00 with offset/remain nonzero
divergences_from_reference.assessment: Same as the reference; optionally restrict BOOT to offset==0 && remain==0. Very unlikely in practice.

upper_layer_requirements: Pass to HID only messages with flags 0x20, command 0x10 and device 1..3. Device 0 with report 0xe0 is the 5-byte status report.

Bound name and string offsets in the device-info and interface-info parsers (payloads can be up to 2038 bytes). Copy the serial into its own buffer, not vendor (reference defect core.c:605), and redact it in logs.
Pair responses to requests by command/report/subdevice; with R2 as is, re-request on an incomplete descriptor within a bounded budget, never an unbounded retry.
